answer: Each agent’s payments can be accepted only after a kernel of independent peers has vouched for its identity over time, with endorsements weighted by the vouched agents’ own track records. A new identity starts at the nadir: it cannot draw on established credit or influence, and repeated endorsements from the same circle add little. To build reach, an attacker must sustain distinct agents and persuade unrelated peers to risk their reputations, tying up resources in a vault of bonds that are forfeited when collusion is exposed.
